question: What is the hundreds digit of \((20!-15!)?\)
solution:
Only the last three digits matter, so look for factors of \(1000\) in the factorials.

The product \(15!=1\cdot2\cdots15\) contains three factors of \(5\) from \(5,10,15\), and at least three factors of \(2\) from \(2,4,6\). Therefore it is divisible by
\[
2^3\cdot5^3=1000.
\]
The product \(20!\) contains all the factors of \(15!\), so it is also divisible by \(1000\). Their difference is consequently a multiple of \(1000\) and ends in \(000\).

The hundreds digit is \(\boxed{0}\), choice \(\text{A}\).
